newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Russia, Georgia in gas supply talks with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Georgia in gas supply talks with Turkey.

text.p: Russia, Turkey, Georgia and Armenia are negotiating a route for possible Russian gas supplies to Turkey via Georgia and Armenia, an official of Georgia's state-owned International Gas Corporation (IGC) of Georgia said on Monday.

Aleksey Gotsiridze, IGC Chairman, said the gas pipeline, if built, might be able to ship up to 9 billion cubic meters (bcm) of natural gas annually from Russia to Turkey across Georgian and possibly Armenian territory.
"The final decision on the route will be taken in October," he said.

Russian officials are considering three main routes, one across Georgia to Turkey, one through both Georgia and Armenia to Turkey, and a third which would avoid both by going from Russia under the Black Sea to Turkey.

The possible gas pipelines through Georgia and Armenia would cost at least $500 million, he said. Rather than building an entirely new line, the projects would involve extending an existing route which already runs from Russia through Georgia and Armenia.
The gas line is currently under-utilised, he said.
He said Russia's giant Gazprom and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) were considering financing the project.
